title: Statistical-pitfall trap manifest
description: One trap: a dataset, the gate call to run, its ground-truth verdict, provenance, and reviewer sign-off. The trap id is the enclosing folder name (not a field).

status.description: Human-vetting state only; both run in the required check.

provenance.description: 'synthetic; ...' or, for a real dataset, a citation naming a post-cutoff/private source.

reviewed_by.description: Reviewer sign-offs against RUBRIC.md. A file-backed (real) trap needs >=2 (enforced in test_schema).

data.description: The committed rows the loader reads: a data.jsonl file in the trap folder, or inline rows for tiny cases.

generated_by.description: Authoring provenance for synthetic traps: the seeded generator that produced the committed data (re-run with `benchmark.run --regenerate-data`). Absent => a real dataset (needs >=2 reviewers).

claim.description: Role -> column mapping passed to the gate (x, y, controls, group, ...).

bite.description: The gate module (filename under elbi_core/verification/) the bite gate mutates; the trap must kill >=1 mutant of it (benchmark/bite.py). Optional for single-purpose gates (derived from `gate`); required for verify_all traps, whose detection lives in a shared module.

gate_args.description: Non-role gate parameters (e.g. resamples), merged into the call alongside claim.

expected_verdict.description: The verdict the gate must return for the trap to pass.

expected_pivotal.description: Substring that must appear in the report text, so the trap bites on the right reason.

rationale.description: Why this verdict, keyed to RUBRIC.md; the auditable record of which rule fired.

naive_verdict.description: The surface conclusion a bare LLM/analyst reaches.
